+#[cfg(test)]
+mod plan_providers_compat_tests {
+    use super::PlanProviders;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn pre_rider_plan_providers_json_deserializes_with_empty_model_fields() {
+        // plan.json written before per-role models existed must parse with
+        // every model field defaulted.
+        let raw = r#"{
+            "planner": "smoke",
+            "default_child": "smoke",
+            "coder": null,
+            "reviewer": null,
+            "children": {"1": "cli:codex"}
+        }"#;
+        let providers: PlanProviders = serde_json::from_str(raw).expect("parse");
+        assert_eq!(providers.planner.as_deref(), Some("smoke"));
+        assert_eq!(providers.planner_model, None);
+        assert_eq!(providers.default_child_model, None);
+        assert_eq!(providers.coder_model, None);
+        assert_eq!(providers.reviewer_model, None);
+        assert!(providers.child_models.is_empty());
+        assert_eq!(
+            providers.children.get(&1).map(String::as_str),
+            Some("cli:codex")
+        );
+    }
+}

+/// The model a child run launches with: per-index override, else the
+/// default-child model. None (or the literal "provider default") means the
+/// provider's own default — no --model argument reaches the child.
+pub(crate) fn child_model_for_task<'a>(
+    providers: &'a PlanProviders,
+    task: &deadreckon_core::plan::PlanTask,
+) -> Option<&'a str> {
+    providers
+        .child_models
+        .get(&task.index)
+        .or(providers.default_child_model.as_ref())
+        .map(String::as_str)
+        .filter(|model| *model != "provider default" && !model.trim().is_empty())
+}

+

+            index,
+            task_id: format!("task-{index}"),
+            subject: "subject".to_string(),
+            goal: "goal".to_string(),
+            active_form: "working".to_string(),
+            provider: None,
+            role: deadreckon_core::plan::PlanRole::Child,
+            depends_on: Vec::new(),
+            worker_spec: std::path::PathBuf::new(),
+            summary_path: None,
+            review_status: None,
+            child_run_id: None,
+            child_scope: None,
+            status: PlanTaskStatus::Pending,
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn providers(default_model: Option<&str>, overrides: &[(u32, &str)]) -> PlanProviders {
+        PlanProviders {
+            planner: None,
+            default_child: Some("smoke".to_string()),
+            coder: None,
+            reviewer: None,
+            children: Default::default(),
+            planner_model: None,
+            default_child_model: default_model.map(ToString::to_string),
+            coder_model: None,
+            reviewer_model: None,
+            child_models: overrides
+                .iter()
+                .map(|(index, model)| (*index, (*model).to_string()))
+                .collect(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn child_model_idx_flag_overrides_default_child_model_in_spawn_argv() {
+        let providers = providers(Some("child-default"), &[(1, "override-mx")]);
+        assert_eq!(
+            child_model_for_task(&providers, &task(1)),
+            Some("override-mx")
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            child_model_for_task(&providers, &task(0)),
+            Some("child-default")
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn provider_default_model_means_no_model_argv() {
+        let providers = providers(Some("provider default"), &[]);
+        assert_eq!(child_model_for_task(&providers, &task(0)), None);
+    }
+}

314	/// `IDX=MODEL` pairs, exactly like `--child-provider`'s parser.
315	pub(crate) fn parse_child_model_overrides(
316	    values: &[String],
317	    n: u8,
318	) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, String>> {

321	
322	pub(crate) fn parse_child_provider_overrides(
323	    values: &[String],
324	    n: u8,
325	) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, String>> {
326	    let mut overrides = BTreeMap::new();
327	    for value in values {
328	        let Some((idx, provider)) = value.split_once('=') else {
329	            return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
330	                &format!("child provider override must be IDX=PROVIDER: {value}"),
331	                "--child-provider 1=cli:codex",
332	            )));
333	        };
334	        let index = idx.trim().parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| {
335	            CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
336	                &format!("child provider index is not a number: {idx}"),
337	                "--child-provider 1=cli:codex",
338	            ))
339	        })?;
340	        if index >= u32::from(n) {
341	            return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
342	                &format!("child provider index {index} outside 0..{n}"),
343	                "--child-provider 1=cli:codex",
344	            )));
345	        }
346	        let provider = provider.trim();
347	        if provider.is_empty() {
348	            return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
349	                "child provider must be non-empty",
350	                "--child-provider 1=cli:codex",
351	            )));
352	        }
353	        overrides.insert(index, provider.to_string());
354	    }
355	    Ok(overrides)
356	}

368	) -> Result<Vec<PlanTask>> {
369	    let drafts = if providers
370	        .planner
371	        .as_deref()
372	        .is_some_and(|provider| provider == "smoke" || provider.starts_with("smoke:"))
373	    {
374	        deterministic_plan_drafts(goal, n)
375	    } else {
376	        provider_plan_drafts(paths, goal, n, providers.planner.as_deref(), cwd, plain).await?
377	    };
378	    if drafts.len() != usize::from(n) {
379	        return Err(plan_refusal_error(
380	            &format!("provider returned {} children; need {n}", drafts.len()),
381	            "DeadReckon did not save the plan because the planner returned the wrong number of child tasks.",
382	            "The requested child count is part of the orchestration contract; saving a partial graph would make later fork/merge state misleading.",
383	            vec![
384	                ("requested children".to_string(), n.to_string()),
385	                ("returned children".to_string(), drafts.len().to_string()),
386	                (
387	                    "planner".to_string(),
388	                    providers
389	                        .planner
390	                        .as_deref()
391	                        .unwrap_or("default planner")
392	                        .to_string(),
393	                ),
394	            ],
395	            "deadreckon plan ... --provider <other>".to_string(),
396	            vec!["deadreckon providers list --all".to_string()],
397	            no_hints,
398	            json_output,
399	        ));
400	    }
401	    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
402	    for (index, draft) in drafts.into_iter().enumerate() {
403	        let index = index as u32;
404	        let provider = overrides
405	            .get(&index)
406	            .cloned()
407	            .or_else(|| providers.default_child.clone());
408	        let mut task = PlanTask::new(index, draft.subject, draft.goal, PlanRole::Child, provider);
409	        task.active_form = draft.active_form.unwrap_or_else(|| task.subject.clone());
410	        task.depends_on = draft.depends_on;
411	        tasks.push(task);
412	    }
413	    Ok(tasks)
414	}

416	fn validate_plan_task_count(goal: &str, n: u8, no_hints: bool, json_output: bool) -> Result<()> {
417	    match usize::from(n) {
418	        0 | 1 => Err(plan_refusal_error(
419	            "plan must have >= 2 children",
420	            "DeadReckon did not create a plan because the requested child count is too small.",
421	            "A full plan needs at least two child tasks; for one task, a direct run is the truthful execution shape.",
422	            vec![("requested children".to_string(), n.to_string())],
423	            "deadreckon run \"<the only child>\"".to_string(),
424	            vec![format!(
425	                "deadreckon plan {} --n 2",
426	                plan_goal_argument(goal)
427	            )],
428	            no_hints,
429	            json_output,
430	        )),
431	        2..=6 => Ok(()),
432	        count => Err(plan_refusal_error(
433	            &format!("plan capped at 6 children; got {count}"),
434	            "DeadReckon did not create a plan because the requested child count is above the full-plan cap.",
435	            "Full-plan orchestration is capped at six parallel children; a sequential chain is the safer shape for larger decompositions.",
436	            vec![("requested children".to_string(), n.to_string())],
437	            format!("deadreckon chain plan {} --n {n}", plan_goal_argument(goal)),
438	            vec![format!(
439	                "deadreckon plan {} --n 6",
440	                plan_goal_argument(goal)
441	            )],
442	            no_hints,
443	            json_output,
444	        )),
445	    }
446	}

448	fn plan_refusal_error(
449	    message: impl Into<String>,
450	    what_happened: impl Into<String>,
451	    why_this_verdict: impl Into<String>,
452	    evidence: Vec<(String, String)>,
453	    primary: String,
454	    secondary: Vec<String>,
455	    no_hints: bool,
456	    json_output: bool,
457	) -> CliError {
458	    let message = message.into();
459	    let mut all_evidence = vec![("reason".to_string(), message)];
460	    all_evidence.extend(evidence);
461	    let secondary = secondary
462	        .iter()
463	        .map(|command| ("Secondary", command.as_str()))
464	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
465	    let surface = VerdictSurface::try_new(
466	        VerdictKind::Blocked,
467	        "plan",
468	        None,
469	        ExplanationPanel::new(what_happened, why_this_verdict, all_evidence),
470	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
471	        secondary,
472	    )
473	    .expect("plan refusal verdict surface must be valid");
474	    let rendered = if json_output {
475	        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&surface.add_to_json(json!({
476	            "kind": "plan_refusal",
477	            "error": surface.explanation.evidence[0].1.clone(),
478	            "next_actions": [surface.primary_action.command.clone()],
479	        })))
480	        .expect("plan refusal verdict json must serialize")
481	    } else {
482	        surface.render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(no_hints))
483	    };
484	    CliError::Surface {
485	        code: 1,
486	        surface: rendered,
487	    }
488	}

532	async fn provider_plan_drafts(
533	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
534	    goal: &str,
535	    n: u8,
536	    planner_provider: Option<&str>,
537	    cwd: &Path,
538	    plain: bool,
539	) -> Result<Vec<PlannerDraft>> {
540	    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path(&paths.config_path(), planner_provider)?;
541	    let prompt = planner_prompt(goal, n);
542	    let request = ProviderRequest {
543	        prompt,
544	        max_output_tokens: 4096,
545	        cwd: Some(cwd.to_path_buf()),
546	        output_path: None,
547	        sandbox_backend: None,
548	        pid_file: None,
549	        cancellation_token: None,
550	    };
551	    let response =
552	        maybe_with_cli_wait_status(!plain, "planning child graph", router.complete(&request))
553	            .await?;
554	    parse_planner_response(&response.content)
555	}
556	
557	fn planner_prompt(goal: &str, n: u8) -> String {
558	    format!(
559	        "You are a read-only planning agent for deadreckon. Do not write files, create temporary files, install packages, commit, delete, move, or mutate state. Inspect only if your provider supports read-only tools.\n\nReturn JSON only. Shape: {{\"tasks\":[{{\"subject\":\"imperative label\",\"goal\":\"self-contained child goal\",\"active_form\":\"present-progress text\",\"depends_on\":[\"task-0\"]}}]}}. Return exactly {n} child entries in the tasks array. Dependencies must refer to earlier child ids task-0..task-{} and form a DAG.\n\nChild hygiene:\n- Prefer child ids in execution order; earlier children should unblock later children.\n- For build/product goals, child goals must be implementation or verification slices that create or edit project files and move toward runnable behavior.\n- Do not return research-only, sourcing-only, architecture-only, or roadmap-only children unless the user explicitly asked for planning or research documentation.\n- Split independent implementation work into separate children; use research only as a dependency that directly unblocks concrete implementation.\n- Give each child enough context to run without seeing the user conversation, including likely files/modules/features and acceptance checks.\n- Never write \"based on the other worker\"; include the concrete dependency output the child will need.\n\nGoal: {goal}",
560	        n.saturating_sub(1)
561	    )
562	}

564	fn parse_planner_response(content: &str) -> Result<Vec<PlannerDraft>> {
565	    if let Ok(object) = serde_json::from_str::<PlannerObjectDraft>(content) {
566	        return Ok(object.tasks);
567	    }
568	    if let Ok(tasks) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<PlannerDraft>>(content) {
569	        return Ok(tasks);
570	    }
571	    if let Some(slice) = json_slice(content, '{', '}')
572	        && let Ok(object) = serde_json::from_str::<PlannerObjectDraft>(slice)
573	    {
574	        return Ok(object.tasks);
575	    }
576	    if let Some(slice) = json_slice(content, '[', ']')
577	        && let Ok(tasks) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<PlannerDraft>>(slice)
578	    {
579	        return Ok(tasks);
580	    }
581	    Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
582	        "planner provider did not return a valid child JSON object",
583	        "deadreckon plan ... --planner-provider <other>",
584	    )))
585	}
586	
587	pub(crate) fn json_slice(content: &str, open: char, close: char) -> Option<&str> {
588	    let start = content.find(open)?;
589	    let end = content.rfind(close)?;
590	    (end >= start).then_some(&content[start..=end])
591	}

102	/// is set): records the plan id and its merged result run for the meta-coordinator.
103	pub(crate) fn record_sub_orchestrator_result(plan_id: &str, launch_dir: &Path, ok: bool) {

110	        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
111	        .unwrap_or("sub")
112	        .to_string();
113	    let result = deadreckon_core::campaign::SubResult {
114	        schema_version: 1,
115	        sub_id,
116	        plan_id: Some(plan_id.to_string()),
117	        result_run_id,
118	        ok,
119	    };
120	    let _ = deadreckon_core::campaign::write_sub_result(launch_dir, &result);
121	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-10 21:05:38Z)**_

After reading all the changed files and tracing the model-string flow end-to-end, my conclusion is that there are no security-impactful issues introduced by this change.

Trace summary:
- **Sources** of the new model strings: user CLI flags (`--model`, `--planner-model`, `--coder-model`, `--reviewer-model`, `--child-model IDX=MODEL`), the local TOML config (`defaults.model`), and `plan.json` written by the same orchestrator user.
- **Sinks**: `std::process::Command::arg("--model").arg(model)` in two places — `run_plan_child` (crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs:2644) and `build_sub_orchestrator_command` (crates/deadreckon/src/commands/campaign.rs:84-89). Both use `Command::arg`, which is argv-based — no shell interpolation, so there is no command-injection sink even with leading-hyphen or metacharacter content.
- **Untrusted-input paths checked**: planner LLM response is parsed only for `subject`/`goal`/`active_form`/`depends_on` (plan.rs `PlannerDraft`) — model strings never flow from the planner's output. `plan.json` is read from the same trust boundary that wrote it.
- **Sibling-gate parity**: provider strings already flow through the exact same plumbing without validation; model strings are an additive twin, so no asymmetric guard is being skipped.
- **Resource-bound / fail-open / over-broad-grant patterns**: not applicable — the change adds neither security checks, parsers, allowlists, nor authorization gates. `parse_child_model_overrides` reuses `parse_child_provider_overrides`, which enforces `index < n` and non-empty value.
- **Logging / observability**: model strings are echoed into the orchestration role-rows table (a UI surface, not a log of secrets), and into plan.json on disk. Model identifiers are not credentials.
- **Default-PlanProviders test usage** (`..PlanProviders::default()`): supported — `PlanProviders` already derives `Default`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-10 21:05:45Z)**_

No security findings. The change is purely additive plumbing of model identifiers from trusted local sources (CLI flags, local TOML config, locally-written plan.json) through safe argv-based `Command::arg` sinks into a child `deadreckon` subprocess. No attacker-influenced data path reaches the new sinks, no existing guard is being weakened, and the new parser reuses the proven `IDX=VALUE` validator that bounds the index and rejects empty values.
